authors.name: Adam Smith
authors.subtitle: Scottish moral philosopher and political economist
authors.bio: Adam Smith (1723-1790) connected moral psychology, commercial society, and political economy in ways that became foundational for classical liberal thought.
authors.bio_pt_br: Adam Smith (1723-1790) conectou psicologia moral, sociedade comercial e economia politica de modo decisivo para o liberalismo classico.

authors.name: Alexis de Tocqueville
authors.subtitle: French analyst of democracy, civil society, and centralization
authors.bio: Alexis de Tocqueville (1805-1859) studied democracy as a social condition, pairing admiration for self-government with warnings about centralization and majority pressure.
authors.bio_pt_br: Alexis de Tocqueville (1805-1859) estudou a democracia como condicao social, admirando o autogoverno e alertando contra centralizacao e tirania da maioria.

authors.name: David Hume
authors.subtitle: Scottish philosopher, essayist, and historian
authors.bio: David Hume (1711-1776) brought skepticism, moral psychology, and institutional realism into debates that deeply shaped liberal political thought.
authors.bio_pt_br: David Hume (1711-1776) levou ceticismo, psicologia moral e realismo institucional a debates que marcaram o pensamento liberal.

authors.name: F. A. Hayek
authors.subtitle: Austrian-British theorist of spontaneous order and rule-based liberty
authors.bio: F. A. Hayek (1899-1992) defended dispersed knowledge, spontaneous order, and constitutional limits against comprehensive planning.
authors.bio_pt_br: F. A. Hayek (1899-1992) defendeu conhecimento disperso, ordem espontanea e limites constitucionais contra o planejamento abrangente.

authors.name: Frederic Bastiat
authors.subtitle: French classical liberal economist and polemic writer
authors.bio: Frederic Bastiat (1801-1850) wrote concise and durable arguments on law, free exchange, protectionism, and the seen and unseen effects of public policy.
authors.bio_pt_br: Frederic Bastiat (1801-1850) escreveu argumentos concisos e duradouros sobre lei, troca livre, protecionismo e efeitos vistos e nao vistos das politicas publicas.

authors.name: Herbert Spencer
authors.subtitle: English individualist theorist of evolution, ethics, and the limits of the state
authors.bio: Herbert Spencer (1820-1903) linked social evolution, individual liberty, and skepticism toward state overreach in a strongly individualist liberal register.
authors.bio_pt_br: Herbert Spencer (1820-1903) articulou evolucao social, liberdade individual e ceticismo quanto a expansao estatal em um registro liberal fortemente individualista.

authors.name: John Locke
authors.subtitle: English philosopher of natural rights and limited government
authors.bio: John Locke (1632-1704) remains central to liberal accounts of consent, rights, property, toleration, and the justified limits of political power.
authors.bio_pt_br: John Locke (1632-1704) segue central para concepcoes liberais de consentimento, direitos, propriedade, tolerancia e limites legitimos do poder politico.

authors.name: John Stuart Mill
authors.subtitle: English liberal philosopher of liberty, individuality, and reform
authors.bio: John Stuart Mill (1806-1873) expanded liberal arguments on individuality, speech, representative institutions, political economy, and social reform.
authors.bio_pt_br: John Stuart Mill (1806-1873) ampliou os argumentos liberais sobre individualidade, liberdade de expressao, instituicoes representativas, economia politica e reforma social.
